proposed.statement:
Consider any collection of i.i.d. triangular sequences in the variance-unrestricted parent class with \(\sigma_n>0\), \(E[\psi_n]=0\), and \(|\psi_n|\le M_\psi\). Suppose, uniformly over that collection,
\[
\widehat\theta_n-\theta_n=\frac1n\sum_{i=1}^n\psi_n(O_{i,n})+O_{P_n}(\delta_n),\qquad
\widehat\sigma_n^2-\sigma_n^2=O_{P_n}(\eta_n),
\]
where
\[
\frac{\sqrt n\,\delta_n}{\sigma_n}\to0,\qquad
\frac{\eta_n}{\sigma_n^2}\to0,\qquad
\sqrt n\,\sigma_n\to\infty
\]
uniformly. Then
\[
\sup_P\sup_{t\in\mathbb R}\left|P_n\!\left(\frac{\sqrt n(\widehat\theta_n-\theta_n)}{\widehat\sigma_n}\le t\right)-\Phi(t)\right|\to0,
\]
\(\widehat\sigma_n/\sigma_n\to1\) uniformly in probability, and the associated Wald intervals have uniform asymptotic coverage \(1-\alpha\). For the frozen one-step decomposition one may take \(\delta_n=r_{q,n}^2+r_{\pi,n}r_{q,n}+n^{-1/2}(r_{\pi,n}+2r_{q,n})\) and \(\eta_n=r_{\pi,n}+2r_{q,n}+n^{-1/2}\), whenever its remainder conclusions hold uniformly on the sequence collection.
proposed.proof_tex:
Write
\[
Z_n=\frac1{\sigma_n\sqrt n}\sum_{i=1}^n\psi_n(O_{i,n}).
\]
For fixed \(t\), Taylor's formula for the complex exponential, \(E[\psi_n]=0\), and \(E[\psi_n^2]=\sigma_n^2\) give
\[
E\exp\left(\frac{it\psi_n}{\sigma_n\sqrt n}\right)
=1-\frac{t^2}{2n}+\rho_n(t),
\]
where
\[
|\rho_n(t)|\le\frac{|t|^3E|\psi_n|^3}{6\sigma_n^3n^{3/2}}
\le\frac{|t|^3M_\psi}{6\sigma_n n^{3/2}}. \tag{1}
\]
The second inequality uses \(|\psi_n|^3\le M_\psi\psi_n^2\). Since \(\sqrt n\,\sigma_n\to\infty\), multiplying the last bound in (1) by \(n\) gives a quantity tending uniformly to zero. Independence within rows therefore yields
\[
E[e^{itZ_n}]
=\left\{1-\frac{t^2}{2n}+\rho_n(t)\right\}^n
\longrightarrow e^{-t^2/2}. \tag{2}
\]
The convergence is uniform over the stated collection. A subsequence argument turns (2) into uniform Kolmogorov convergence: if uniform convergence of distribution functions failed, choose a violating sequence of laws; (2) along that sequence gives weak convergence to the continuous standard-normal distribution, which implies convergence in Kolmogorov distance, a contradiction. Thus
\[
\sup_P\sup_t|P_n(Z_n\le t)-\Phi(t)|\to0. \tag{3}
\]

The variance condition and positivity of \(\sigma_n\) give
\[
\left|\frac{\widehat\sigma_n}{\sigma_n}-1\right|
=\frac{|\widehat\sigma_n^2-\sigma_n^2|}{\sigma_n(\widehat\sigma_n+\sigma_n)}
\le\frac{|\widehat\sigma_n^2-\sigma_n^2|}{\sigma_n^2}
=o_{P_n}(1) \tag{4}
\]
uniformly. In particular, \(P_n(\widehat\sigma_n>0)\to1\) uniformly. If \(R_n\) denotes the estimator remainder, the first relative-rate condition gives
\[
\frac{\sqrt nR_n}{\sigma_n}=o_{P_n}(1). \tag{5}
\]
On the event of a positive denominator, the studentized statistic equals
\[
\frac{Z_n+\sqrt nR_n/\sigma_n}{\widehat\sigma_n/\sigma_n}.
\]
Equations (3)--(5), using the same subsequence argument for uniformity, prove the asserted uniform standard-normal limit. The frozen zero-denominator convention changes the statistic only on an event of uniformly vanishing probability. Evaluating the limit at \(\pm z_{1-\alpha/2}\) gives
\[
P_n\!\left(\theta_n\in\left[\widehat\theta_n\mathbin\pm z_{1-\alpha/2}\widehat\sigma_n/\sqrt n\right]\right)\to1-\alpha
\]
uniformly. If the stated one-step remainder and variance bounds hold, the final assertion follows by substituting their deterministic upper envelopes into the two relative-rate conditions.

proposed.statement: Let \(Z_1,Z_2,\ldots\) be independent \(N(0,1)\) variables and let \(\lambda_1,\lambda_2,\ldots\in\mathbb R\). The centered quadratic series \(\sum_{j\ge1}\lambda_j(Z_j^2-1)\) converges in \(L^2\) if and only if \(\sum_{j\ge1}\lambda_j^2<\infty\). If \(\lambda_j\ge0\), the uncentered series \(\sum_{j\ge1}\lambda_jZ_j^2\) converges in \(L^1\) if and only if \(\sum_{j\ge1}\lambda_j<\infty\). For a family \(\Lambda\) of square-summable sequences, common rank-\(J\) truncations approximate the centered series uniformly in \(L^2\) if and only if \(\lim_{J\to\infty}\sup_{\lambda\in\Lambda}\sum_{j>J}\lambda_j^2=0\). If \(\lambda_j=\lambda_\circ>0\) for infinitely many \(j\), the centered partial sums have no weakly convergent subsequence.
proposed.proof_tex:
Put \(S_J=\sum_{j=1}^J\lambda_j(Z_j^2-1)\).  Independence, centering, and \(E[(Z_j^2-1)^2]=2\) give, whenever \(J>L\),
\[
E[(S_J-S_L)^2]=2\sum_{j=L+1}^J\lambda_j^2. \tag{1}
\]
Thus \((S_J)\) is Cauchy in \(L^2\) if and only if \(\sum_j\lambda_j^2<\infty\), which proves the first assertion by completeness of \(L^2\).  The same identity uniformly over \(\lambda\in\Lambda\) gives
\[
\sup_{\lambda\in\Lambda}E\!\left[\left\{\sum_{j>J}\lambda_j(Z_j^2-1)\right\}^2\right]
=2\sup_{\lambda\in\Lambda}\sum_{j>J}\lambda_j^2,
\]
and proves the common-truncation criterion in both directions.

If \(\lambda_j\ge0\), the uncentered partial sums increase almost surely and
\[
E\!\left[\sum_{j\ge1}\lambda_jZ_j^2\right]=\sum_{j\ge1}\lambda_j. \tag{2}
\]
When the right side is finite, the expected nonnegative tail tends to zero, so the partial sums converge in \(L^1\).  Conversely, \(L^1\) convergence bounds their expectations, and (2) forces \(\sum_j\lambda_j<\infty\).

For the last assertion, the characteristic function of the actual full centered partial sum is
\[
\varphi_{S_J}(t)=\prod_{j\le J}e^{-it\lambda_j}(1-2it\lambda_j)^{-1/2},
\qquad
|\varphi_{S_J}(t)|=\prod_{j\le J}(1+4t^2\lambda_j^2)^{-1/4}. \tag{3}
\]
Let \(m_J=|\{j\le J:\lambda_j=\lambda_\circ\}|\).  By hypothesis \(m_J\to\infty\), and every factor in (3) is at most one.  Hence, for every \(t\ne0\),
\[
|\varphi_{S_J}(t)|
\le(1+4t^2\lambda_\circ^2)^{-m_J/4}\longrightarrow0. \tag{4}
\]
Suppose some full-partial-sum subsequence \(S_{J_r}\) converged weakly to a real random variable \(S\).  Since \(x\mapsto e^{itx}\) is bounded and continuous, weak convergence would give \(\varphi_{S_{J_r}}(t)\to E[e^{itS}]\) for every \(t\).  Equation (4) would therefore imply \(E[e^{itS}]=0\) for every \(t\ne0\).  But dominated convergence gives \(E[e^{itS}]\to1\) as \(t\to0\), a contradiction.  Thus the actual full partial sums have no weakly convergent subsequence.
proposed.justification: The full centered partial sums are controlled by their actual characteristic-function product, not by a selected subseries.
proposed.gap: A selected-subseries argument does not by itself exclude convergence of the full partial sums.
proposed.consumer: It supplies the exact spectral compactness criterion and the full-partial-sum obstruction used by the degeneracy theorem.

\]
with efficiency bound \(\sigma_n^2=E_{P_n}[\psi_n^2]\).  For any predetermined \(\mathscr C\subseteq\mathscr P^{\mathrm{vs}}_{\sigma_\star}\) on which the displayed density and propensity learner rates hold, the explicit cross-fitted coupled wavelet--Brenier one-step estimator \(\widehat\theta_n\) and studentizer \(\widehat\sigma_n\) satisfy
\[
\frac{\sqrt n(\widehat\theta_n-\theta_n)}{\widehat\sigma_n}\Rightarrow N(0,1)
\]
uniformly over \(\mathscr C\), attain the efficiency bound, and give two-sided Wald coverage tending uniformly to \(1-\alpha\).  The variance-unrestricted parent \(\mathscr P^{\mathrm{vu}}\) remains separate and permits equality.  At equality the first-order gradient vanishes; the proved spectral theorem obstructs only the unregularized \(n\)-scale full-tangent Gaussian calibration route.  A broadly honest degeneracy-adaptive procedure, including slower regularized or other derivative-aware constructions, remains open.

prose_updates.interpretation: The causal object of interest is the lower endpoint \(\theta_n\), not the generally unidentified moment \(E[\lVert Y_n(1)-Y_n(0)\rVert_2^2]\) itself.  The canonical gradient contains a covariate-composition term \(V_n(X)-\theta_n\) and one inverse-propensity centered transport derivative for the realized arm.  On a predetermined variance-separated collection with valid nuisance-rate premises, \(\widehat\theta_n\) is asymptotically linear with this influence function, \(\widehat\sigma_n\) consistently estimates its efficiency-bound standard deviation, and the two-sided interval \([\widehat\theta_n\mathbin\pm z_{1-\alpha/2}\widehat\sigma_n/\sqrt n]\) has uniform limiting coverage \(1-\alpha\).  In a 401(k) SIPP application, this interpretation requires credible ignorability, overlap, support and Brenier regularity, nuisance learning rates, and variance separation.
prose_updates.technical_internal_limitation: The regular theorem is intentionally uniform only over predetermined \(\mathscr C\subseteq\mathscr P^{\mathrm{vs}}_{\sigma_\star}\). This rules out a uniformly tight unregularized \(n\)-scale Gaussian spectral calibration over the full parent.  It does not rule out slower covariate-regularized, derivative-aware, subsampling, or other honest adaptive procedures; constructing and validating such a procedure remains open.
prose_updates.honest_scope: Sharp causal identification uses consistency, conditional ignorability, fixed overlap, and measurable attainment of the conditional optimal coupling.  Canonical-gradient validity is pointwise at regular-support laws in the full nonparametric observed-data tangent space.  Uniform root-\(n\) inference additionally requires a predetermined collection inside \(\mathscr P^{\mathrm{vs}}_{\sigma_\star}\), the stated support, density, and all-feasible-pairs Brenier conditions, and density and propensity learner rates imposed as estimator-side premises over that collection.  The primitive H\"older proposition verifies those rates only on \(\mathscr P^{\mathrm{vs,H}}_{\sigma_\star,t_\pi,L_\pi}\).  No claim is made under hidden confounding, overlap failure, nonsmooth or unbounded supports, or for a single honest procedure uniformly adaptive across all positive-variance sequences and equality.  The degeneracy theorem is a partial route obstruction, not a solution of that broad open problem.
